varieties.name: Reinette Clochard
varieties.summary: Firm, juicy, sweet flesh; a very long-keeping winter apple that stays good into March, though it shrivels and softens toward the end of storage.

varieties.name: Reinette Grise du Canada
varieties.summary: Fine, dense, lightly crisp flesh that is juicy, sweet and pleasantly sharp, with a good perfume. Excellent for purées and baking, where it breaks down into a tangy fluff; keeps rather less well than the smooth-skinned form.

varieties.name: Rescue
varieties.summary: Crisp and juicy with a tart-sweet balance, good eaten fresh from the tree; it turns mealy within a few weeks. Also used for sauce and preserves.

varieties.name: Reverend W. Wilks
varieties.summary: Crisp, fine-grained, juicy white flesh with a mild sweet-sharp balance. It cooks quickly to a pale yellow froth or smooth purée that needs little sugar. The flesh browns very fast once cut.

varieties.name: Rhode Island Greening
varieties.summary: Firm, juicy flesh with a strong, clean sharpness; hard and tart fresh off the tree but richer after storage. Cooked, it keeps its shape and develops a full, sweet-tart flavour, making it a classic American pie apple.

varieties.name: Ribston Pippin
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-grained flesh with an intense, rich, aromatic flavour that is sharper and more robust than Cox, with some pear-like notes. Best a few weeks after picking; also good for cooking and juice.

varieties.name: Rome Beauty
varieties.summary: Firm, slightly coarse and moderately juicy flesh with a mild, gently sweet-tart flavour and little perfume when raw. Its real strength is in the oven: it holds its shape when baked whole and the flavour deepens with cooking.

varieties.name: Rosemary Russet
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-grained and juicy, with a lively balance of sugar and acid and a rich, aromatic finish. Sharper than most russets when first picked, it rounds out and sweetens after a few weeks in store.

varieties.name: Ross Nonpareil
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp and on the dry side, with plenty of sugar and a rich, aromatic flavour that old writers likened to the fennel-scented Fenouillet apples, giving it a faint anise note.

varieties.name: Roxbury Russet
varieties.summary: Firm, somewhat coarse yellowish flesh, sugary yet tart, with a rich, slightly spicy character that improves after a few weeks in store. Makes a sweet, high-sugar juice and cider.

varieties.name: Royal Gala
varieties.summary: Sweet and gentle with little acidity and a light floral, pear-like scent; crisp rather than hard, with thin skin and juicy cream flesh. Best fresh off the tree - the flavour is pleasant but simple, and after long storage it fades and the texture can turn mealy.

varieties.name: Royal Jubilee
varieties.summary: Firm, yellow, medium-coarse flesh with a moderate sub-acid taste. A sound cooker of no special aroma.

varieties.name: Rubens
varieties.summary: Crisp and juicy with a good blend of sweetness and lively acidity, often described as almost fizzy on the tongue; more aromatic than Gala, showing some of Elstar's character.

varieties.name: Rubinette
varieties.summary: Rich, intense sweet-sharp flavour with Cox-like aromatics and a juicy, crisp bite; widely rated among the best-flavoured modern apples, and more consistent from year to year than Cox.

varieties.name: Rubinola
varieties.summary: Sweet with balancing acidity and a good aroma; the cream flesh is crisp but light and juicy, and slow to brown when cut.

varieties.name: Saltcote Pippin
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp cream flesh that is only moderately juicy, with a sweet, pleasantly aromatic flavour.

varieties.name: Sam Young
varieties.summary: Firm, rather tough greenish flesh; older descriptions call it sugary and highly flavoured, while modern NFC notes describe a milder, subacid taste.

varieties.name: Sansa
varieties.summary: Sweet, juicy and crisp-tender in the Gala style, with a little more acidity from Akane to keep it lively. An early apple to eat soon after picking.

varieties.name: Santana
varieties.summary: A delicately perfumed apple with a vinous sweet-sharp balance, compared with Spartan; some tasters find hints of rose, lychee or sweet grape. Creamy-yellow flesh is firm and juicy rather than crunchy, and it does not keep long.

varieties.name: Saturn
varieties.summary: Crisp flesh that snaps cleanly and is very juicy. Clearly sweet but balanced by a good measure of acidity, so it tastes properly of apple rather than just sugary.

varieties.name: Schöner aus Nordhausen
varieties.summary: A sharp, finely aromatic late keeper, used both for eating once it mellows in store and in the kitchen.

varieties.name: Scotch Bridget
varieties.summary: Soft, tender white flesh, juicy with a lively acidity. Cooks well, and after a couple of months in store it mellows enough to be eaten raw in the new year.

varieties.name: Scrumptious
varieties.summary: Sweet but well balanced by a fresh acidity, with the strawberry hint of its Discovery and Worcester ancestry and sometimes a faint aniseed note. Thin skin and white flesh that snaps cleanly at first but goes soft and floury if left on the tree too long.

varieties.name: Self-Fertile Cox
varieties.summary: Tastes like Cox's Orange Pippin: rich and aromatic with honeyed sweetness, floral and pear-drop notes and balancing acidity. Some growers find heavy self-set crops give smaller fruit with slightly less depth.

varieties.name: Sheepnose
varieties.summary: Greenish-white, firm, coarse flesh that is sweet, mild in acid and notably aromatic, with a dry, nutty quality. It turns dry and fibrous if over-ripe or stored long, so it is best used fairly soon; traditionally baked or dried.

varieties.name: Shenandoah
varieties.summary: Crisp, juicy, yellowish flesh with a sweet, lightly perfumed flavour; pleasant raw but at its most useful in the kitchen, where slices hold their shape.

varieties.name: Siberian Crab
varieties.summary: Small, sharp and somewhat astringent; one grower notes a fleeting sweet, rosy start followed by a dry, bitter finish. Cooks to a pink-tinged sauce and makes good jelly.

varieties.name: Signe Tillisch
varieties.summary: Juicy, sweet and only mildly acidic, with the soft, tender texture of the Calville group; best for a few weeks in late autumn.

varieties.name: Sima Joon
varieties.summary: A crisp late apple whose flavour is described as an even balance of sweetness and acidity. Early reports only; it has had very little independent tasting.

varieties.name: Sir Prize
varieties.summary: Tender, very juicy cream flesh with a sweet, lightly scented Golden Delicious-type flavour. Good for eating fresh and for baking, but the fruit bruises badly in handling.

varieties.name: Slack Ma Girdle
varieties.summary: Very sweet, soft and tender with little acid or tannin; pleasant to eat fresh and used in cider to add sugar, with some makers noting a woody note.

varieties.name: Smokehouse
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp, moderately fine-grained yellowish flesh with a pleasant balance of sweetness and acidity, a gently spicy, honeyed note and a fresh-cider character. Good raw and very good for pies and baking.

varieties.name: Snowsweet
varieties.summary: Sweet, with just enough tartness for balance and a rich, rounded, almost savoury depth. Flesh is crisp-tender and juicy, and slices stay white long after cutting.

varieties.name: Spartan
varieties.summary: Snow-white, crisp and juicy flesh with a sweet, gently vinous McIntosh character and low acidity. Very good fresh from the tree but softens and loses crunch if kept too long or grown too large.

varieties.name: St Edmund's Pippin
varieties.summary: Juicy, fine-textured cream flesh, firm when picked, with a sweet, rich flavour often likened to pear and a touch of acidity. It is at its best within a few weeks and turns soft and dull if kept.

varieties.name: St Helens
varieties.summary: A dark red early dessert apple with a crisp, light texture. A taster found it floral and sugary, a lighter style than the nursery's other early seedling.

varieties.name: Statefair
varieties.summary: Juicy and crisp with a firmer bite than most summer apples, and a tart-sweet, mildly aromatic flavour that leans to the sharp side.

varieties.name: Stayman Winesap
varieties.summary: Fine-grained, tender and very juicy flesh with a brisk, tart-sweet, spicy, wine-like flavour that recalls its Winesap parent but is softer in texture. Sharp at picking, it mellows after a few weeks in store.

varieties.name: Stirling Castle
varieties.summary: Very soft, coarse, juicy white flesh with plenty of acidity. Cooks quickly to a sharp, fluffy puree.

varieties.name: Sturmer Pippin
varieties.summary: Very firm, crisp and juicy. Hard and sharp when first picked, it slowly sweetens in store and by late winter is rich and brisk, still with plenty of acidity.

varieties.name: Summer Rambo
varieties.summary: Coarse, tender, breaking flesh that is exceptionally juicy, with a mildly tart, sweet-sharp, slightly honeyed flavour. Good fresh straight off the tree and very good for sauce, pies and frying; it softens quickly.

varieties.name: Sunrise
varieties.summary: Remarkably crisp for an August apple, with juicy white flesh and a balanced sweet-sharp flavour that some tasters liken to strawberry. Best chilled and eaten within a week or so of picking.

varieties.name: Sunset
varieties.summary: Crisp, fine, cream flesh with a sweet, aromatic Cox-like flavour and gentle acidity. In good summers it rivals Cox; in dull years it is still sweet and crisp but less complex.

varieties.name: Suntan
varieties.summary: Firm, slightly coarse, moderately juicy cream flesh with an intense, aromatic flavour in the Cox mould but noticeably sharper. It mellows after some weeks in store.

varieties.name: Swaar
varieties.summary: Dense, fine-grained creamy flesh that is sweet and richly aromatic with a nutty depth, the qualities that made its name among 19th-century American growers. Best after a spell in store.
